title: Coupler-owned fixed-allocation management boundary scheduler
problem: Ribasim v2026.1.1 fixed allocation boundaries crossed inside one BMI update_until are not guaranteed to execute. The outer coupler must therefore split requested advances at explicit allocation boundaries and preserve that scheduling state over restart.
scope: Implement deterministic boundary scheduling only. Do not execute Ribasim, change allocation policy, recommend a universal timestep or characterize new clock lattices.
state_machine: At an unsolved allocation boundary the clock is BOUNDARY_PENDING and physical advance is forbidden.
mark_boundary_solved publishes that management solve as completed and advances the next boundary index.
accept_advance moves only to the planned target; reaching the allocation boundary makes BOUNDARY_PENDING again.
A request crossing multiple boundaries must iterate plan/accept/solve until its requested target is reached.
requirements: The scheduler never advances across a pending allocation boundary.
The A5 case emits exact 5 h allocation boundaries even though product targets are 6 h apart.
The aligned A6 case introduces no extra non-product physical target.
Same clock state plus same requested target produces identical plans.
Accepting a target different from the current plan fails closed.
Restart persistence reconstructs current time, next boundary index and pending/solved state exactly.
A restart on a pending boundary cannot skip that allocation solve.
A restart after a solved boundary cannot repeat the previous allocation solve.
nonclaims: No real Ribasim trajectory equivalence yet; that is the next qualification boundary.
No production admission by RM11 alone.
